mainTopic: Blood in the פרוזדור (inside or outside the לול, floor or roof), and רבי יוחנן's list of three cases where חכמים treated a רוב as certain.
overview: The amud opens by noting that אביי's version that follows the חזקה disagrees with רב קטינא. רבי חייא says blood found in the פרוזדור is definitely impure, while רב קטינא says it is impure only out of doubt. According to רב הונא they don't argue: one is talking about blood inside the לול, the other about blood outside it. רמי בר שמואל and רב יצחק בריה דרב יהודה say blood outside the לול is pure, so for them both rulings must be about the inner area. The גמרא answers that רבי חייא means blood on the floor of the פרוזדור and רב קטינא means blood on its roof. Then רבי יוחנן teaches that in three cases, מקור, שליא and חתיכה, חכמים followed the רוב and treated it as certain. The גמרא challenges his list with the nine stores and the nine frogs, and answers by narrowing the list first to טומאה and then to a woman's טומאה. At the end, it starts a new challenge from רבי יהושע בן לוי about a woman who crossed a river, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: אביי's חזקה version clashes with רב קטינא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that אביי's version that follows the חזקה, which supports רבי חייא, disagrees with רב קטינא, who holds the blood is impure only out of doubt.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this disagrees with רב קטינא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that אביי's version that follows the חזקה argues with רב קטינא. This sets up the next steps, which try to settle the clash.
steps.deeperAnalysis: As רש״י explains, in that version there is no impurity out of doubt at all. From the לול inward the blood is definitely impure, and from the לול outward it is definitely pure. רב קטינא, though, treats blood in the פרוזדור as impure only because of a ספק, so the two clash.

keyTerms.meaning: It disagrees (with someone)
The outer passage of the woman's body, between the inner chamber and the outside

phrases.english: And it disagrees with Rav Ketina.
phrases.notes: "It" means אביי's version that follows the חזקה, the one that just backed רבי חייא. In that version nothing here is a ספק, and that's what clashes with רב קטינא.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Observes a conflict between אביי's חזקה version, which was just shown to support רבי חייא, and רב קטינא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אביי's חזקה version (no impurity out of doubt) disagrees with רב קטינא (impure out of doubt) about blood in the פרוזדור.

steps.title: According to רב הונא, they are talking about different spots
steps.stepSummary: Using רב הונא's view, the גמרא explains that רבי חייא and רב קטינא don't really argue. One is talking about blood inside the לול, the other about blood outside it.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to רב הונא, they don't disagree. Here (רבי חייא) is about blood found from the לול inward, and there (רב קטינא) is about blood found from the לול outward.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא settles the clash by splitting the פרוזדור into two areas, following רב הונא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא holds that blood inside the לול is definitely impure, and blood outside it is impure out of doubt. So רבי חייא's 'definitely impure' fits the inner area, and רב קטינא's 'impure out of doubt' fits the outer area. Both are right, each about a different spot.

keyTerms.meaning: They do not disagree
Here... there: the classic way of splitting two rulings into two different cases
A point in the פרוזדור that splits it into an inner and an outer area
Inward / outward

steps.confusionAlert: Both 'כאן' are short. The first one points to רבי חייא (definitely impure), and the second to רב קטינא (impure out of doubt).

phrases.english: According to Rav Huna, they do not disagree:
here, from the lul inward,
phrases.notes: This is רבי חייא's case, where the blood is definitely impure.

phrases.english: there, from the lul outward.
phrases.notes: This is רב קטינא's case, where the blood is impure only out of doubt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the conflict raised in step 1.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (כאן... כאן) by location in the פרוזדור
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי חייא and רב קטינא argue about the same blood.
steps.terutzMaskana: According to רב הונא, each one is talking about a different area (inside or outside the לול), so there is no argument.

steps.title: What about רמי בר שמואל and רב יצחק?
steps.stepSummary: רמי בר שמואל and רב יצחק בריה דרב יהודה say blood outside the לול is pure out of doubt, and blood inside is impure out of doubt. So where can the רבי חייא and רב קטינא rulings be placed?
steps.simpleTranslation: But according to רמי בר שמואל and רב יצחק בריה דרב יהודה, who say that from the לול outward, its doubt is pure, and from the לול inward, its doubt is impure, how are these rulings explained?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא checks whether רב הונא's neat split also works for another opinion. It asks where the rulings could be placed according to that view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For these אמוראים, blood outside the לול is not impure at all, so רב קטינא's 'impure out of doubt' cannot be about the outer area. That ruins the split from step 2.

keyTerms.meaning: When in doubt, it is pure
When in doubt, it is impure
In what case can it be set up / explained?

phrases.english: But according to Rami bar Shmuel

phrases.aramaic: וּלְרַב יִצְחָק בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוּדָה, דְּאָמְרִי:
phrases.english: and Rav Yitzchak son of Rav Yehuda, who say:
from the lul outward, its doubt is pure,
from the lul inward, its doubt is impure,
in what case can these be set up?
phrases.notes: "These" are the rulings of רבי חייא and רב קטינא.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא לְרָמֵי בַּר שְׁמוּאֵל וּלְרַב יִצְחָק בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the step 2 answer against a different opinion about the לול.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Where in the פרוזדור the rulings of רבי חייא and רב קטינא can be placed, according to רמי בר שמואל and רב יצחק.

steps.title: Both must be about blood inside the לול
steps.stepSummary: The answer: according to these אמוראים, both rulings must be about blood found from the לול inward.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its own question. Both rulings must be talking about the inner area.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Blood outside the לול is pure for these אמוראים, so it cannot be the case of either ruling. Only the inner area is left, and that sets up a problem in the next step.

phrases.english: From the lul inward.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The rulings must be about blood found from the לול inward.

steps.title: Do they then argue with רבי חייא?
steps.stepSummary: If so, רמי בר שמואל and רב יצחק say blood inside the לול is impure only out of doubt, but רבי חייא says it is definitely impure. Shall we say they argue with him?
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say that they disagree with רבי חייא?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a challenge: these אמוראים now seem to argue with the ברייתא of רבי חייא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Inside the לול, רמי בר שמואל and רב יצחק say 'impure out of doubt', while רבי חייא says 'definitely impure'. An אמורא normally should not argue with a תנא like רבי חייא, so this is a real problem the גמרא will need to answer.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say? The opening of a suggestion the גמרא will usually try to push away

steps.whatToRemember: רב הונא's view makes peace between רבי חייא and רב קטינא by splitting inside and outside the לול. The view of רמי בר שמואל and רב יצחק cannot use that split, so it seems to clash with רבי חייא.

phrases.english: Shall we say it disagrees with Rabbi Chiyya!
phrases.notes: "It" is the view of רמי בר שמואל and רב יצחק: inside the לול, the blood is only impure out of doubt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a problem out of the answer in step 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view of רמי בר שמואל and רב יצחק בריה דרב יהודה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: For blood inside the לול, they say impure out of doubt, but רבי חייא says definitely impure, so they seem to argue with a ברייתא.

steps.title: Floor of the corridor versus roof of the corridor
steps.stepSummary: There is no real argument. רבי חייא (definitely impure) speaks of blood found on the floor of the פרוזדור. רב קטינא (impure only out of doubt) speaks of blood found on its roof.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not a problem. Here, the blood was found on the floor of the corridor. There, it was found on the roof of the corridor.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 5. It says רמי בר שמואל and רב יצחק don't have to argue with רבי חייא, because each ruling is about a different spot.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even inside the לול, the exact spot matters. Blood on the floor of the פרוזדור is assumed to come from the מקור, so רבי חייא calls it definitely impure. Blood on the roof could have come from somewhere else, so רב קטינא calls it impure only out of doubt.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult. The opening words of an answer.
The floor of the corridor (the passage of the woman's body)
The roof (upper side) of the corridor

steps.whatToRemember: Inside the לול: blood on the floor is ודאי טמא (רבי חייא). Blood on the roof is טמא only out of doubt (רב קטינא).

phrases.english: It is not difficult.
Here, it is where the blood was found on the floor of the corridor,
phrases.notes: "Here" is רבי חייא's ruling, the one that says definitely impure.

phrases.english: and there, it is where it was found on the roof of the corridor.
phrases.notes: "There" is רב קטינא's ruling, impure only out of doubt.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא, כָּאן כְּשֶׁנִּמְצָא בַּקַּרְקַע פְּרוֹזְדוֹר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 5 by splitting the area inside the לול into floor and roof.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the case (אוקימתא): two rulings about two different spots
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought רמי בר שמואל and רב יצחק, who say blood inside the לול is impure only out of doubt, must argue with רבי חייא.
steps.terutzMaskana: No argument. Floor blood is ודאי טמא and roof blood is ספק טמא, so all the opinions fit together.

steps.title: Three places where חכמים treated a רוב as a certainty
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן teaches that in three cases, מקור, שליא and חתיכה, חכמים followed the רוב and treated it as ודאי. The case of מקור is the one just discussed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: in three places חכמים followed the רוב and treated it as certain: the מקור, the שליא, and the חתיכה (a shaped limb). The מקור is what we just said.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן gives a new general rule and lists three cases. He explains the first one right away, by pointing back to the blood we just discussed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually a doubt stays a doubt. In these three cases חכמים relied on what usually happens (the רוב) and ruled as if it were certain. The מקור case: blood found from the לול inward (on the floor) is ruled definitely impure, because most blood there comes from the מקור.

keyTerms.meaning: They followed the majority (what usually happens)
A certainty, as opposed to a doubt (ספק)
The source, meaning the uterus, where impure blood comes from
The afterbirth (placenta / birth sac)
A shaped limb, a hand or foot with a clear form

steps.whyThisMatters: This turns the specific blood case into a broad principle: a strong רוב can be treated like full certainty, not just as a reason to be strict.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
In three places
the Sages followed the majority,
and made them like a certainty:
the source, the afterbirth, and a shaped limb.
The source is what we just said;
phrases.notes: He means the blood in the פרוזדור we were just discussing. Most blood there comes from the מקור.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: בִּשְׁלֹשָׁה מְקוֹמוֹת הָלְכוּ בּוֹ חֲכָמִים אַחַר הָרוֹב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the result of step 6 as the first example of a wider rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In the cases of מקור, שליא and חתיכה, חכמים followed the רוב and ruled as if it were ודאי.

steps.title: The afterbirth case: no afterbirth without a baby
steps.stepSummary: The source for שליא: an afterbirth in a house makes the house impure. This is not because the afterbirth itself is a baby, but because there is usually no afterbirth without a baby. רבי שמעון disagrees: the baby dissolved before it came out.
steps.simpleTranslation: The afterbirth, as we learned: if an afterbirth is in a house, the house is impure. This is not because the afterbirth is a baby, but because there is no afterbirth without a baby. רבי שמעון says: the baby dissolved before it came out.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a משנה to show the second of רבי יוחנן's three cases, the שליא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We never see a baby, only the afterbirth. But since an afterbirth almost always holds a baby, חכמים treat it as certain that a dead baby is there, and that brings טומאת מת to the whole house. רבי שמעון holds the baby fell apart before it came out, so he does not reach the same result.

keyTerms.meaning: The house is impure. Everything under the roof gets corpse impurity (טומאת אהל).
A baby / fetus
Dissolved, broke down

phrases.english: The afterbirth, as we learned in a משנה:
If an afterbirth is in a house, the house is impure,
not because the afterbirth itself is a baby,
but because there is no afterbirth without a baby.
Rabbi Shimon says:
The baby dissolved before it came out.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the second item on רבי יוחנן's list.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוחנן's claim that שליא is a case where רוב is treated as ודאי
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה: "שליא בבית הבית טמא... שאין שליא בלא ולד"

steps.title: The shaped limb case: we assume a normal baby
steps.stepSummary: The source for חתיכה: a woman who miscarries a shaped hand or foot has the impurity of a woman who gave birth. We don't worry that it came from a baby with a sealed (deficient) body.
steps.simpleTranslation: A shaped limb, as we learned: a woman who miscarries a shaped hand or a shaped foot, her status is impure from giving birth. We don't worry that it may have come from a sealed body.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a source for the third case on רבי יוחנן's list, the חתיכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A miscarried limb could in theory come from a deformed fetus (גוף אטום), which would not count as a birth. Since most fetuses are normal, חכמים follow the רוב and treat it as a certain birth, so the mother gets טומאת לידה.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman who miscarries
Impure with the impurity of a woman who gave birth
A sealed body, a deformed fetus that does not count as a real birth
We are not concerned (we don't worry about this possibility)

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן's three cases of רוב treated as ודאי: מקור (blood is from the uterus), שליא (an afterbirth has a baby), and חתיכה (a limb is from a normal fetus).

phrases.english: A shaped limb, as we learned:
A woman who miscarries a shaped hand or a shaped foot,
phrases.notes: "Shaped" means it has a clear form, like fingers you can see. It does not mean cut off.

phrases.english: its mother is impure with the impurity of birth,

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵין חוֹשְׁשִׁין שֶׁמָּא מִגּוּף אָטוּם בָּאת.
phrases.english: and we are not concerned that perhaps it came from a sealed body.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the third and last item on רבי יוחנן's list.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוחנן's claim that חתיכה is a case where רוב is treated as ודאי
steps.raayaSupportSource: "המפלת יד חתוכה ורגל חתוכה אמו טמאה לידה ואין חוששין שמא מגוף אטום באת"

steps.title: Isn't the case of nine stores missing from the list?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether רבי יוחנן's list of three is complete. It brings a ברייתא about nine kosher stores and one נבלה store, where found meat follows the רוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: Are there really no more cases? There is also the case of nine stores! A ברייתא teaches: nine stores sell kosher slaughtered meat and one sells נבלה meat. If a person bought from one of them and doesn't know which one, the doubtful meat is forbidden. But if meat is found in the street, follow the majority.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי יוחנן's list of three cases. It points to another case where חכמים also followed the רוב: meat found near nine kosher stores and one non-kosher store.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן said there are only three cases where the רוב is treated as certain. The ברייתא shows a fourth: meat found in the street is treated as kosher because most stores are kosher. So the list seems incomplete.

keyTerms.meaning: Nine stores: the classic case of a majority of kosher meat sellers
Meat from an animal that was properly slaughtered (kosher)
Meat from an animal that died without proper slaughter (forbidden)
In this case of doubt, the meat is forbidden
Something found, here meat found away from the stores
Follow the majority

steps.confusionAlert: The challenge comes from the SECOND half of the ברייתא, the found meat that follows the רוב. It does not come from the first half, where the bought meat is forbidden.

phrases.english: And are there no more?
phrases.notes: More cases beyond רבי יוחנן's three: מקור, שליא and חתיכה.

phrases.english: But there is the case of nine stores!
As it is taught in a ברייתא:

phrases.aramaic: תֵּשַׁע חֲנוּיוֹת, כּוּלָּן מוֹכְרוֹת בְּשַׂר שְׁחוּטָה,
phrases.english: Nine stores, all of which sell slaughtered meat,
and one store sells נבלה meat,
and a person bought from one of them
and he does not know which one he bought from:
this case of doubt is forbidden.
phrases.notes: He bought it right at the store, where the stores stay fixed in place, so here we don't follow the majority.

phrases.english: And in the case of found meat:
follow the majority.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the completeness of רבי יוחנן's list after the sources for all three cases were shown.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's claim that there are only three cases where חכמים followed the רוב as ודאי.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא of תשע חנויות shows another case where found meat is treated as kosher based on the רוב, so the list seems to be missing a case.

steps.title: The list covers only impurity, not prohibitions
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רבי יוחנן was listing only cases of טומאה. The nine-stores case is about איסור, so it does not belong on his list.
steps.simpleTranslation: We are talking about טומאה. We are not talking about איסור.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. רבי יוחנן's list was only about ritual impurity, so a case about forbidden food was never meant to be included.
steps.deeperAnalysis: All three of רבי יוחנן's cases (מקור, שליא, חתיכה) deal with טומאה. The nine-stores case deals with whether meat is forbidden to eat, which is איסור. So the list is complete within its own topic.

keyTerms.meaning: Ritual impurity
A prohibition, such as forbidden food
We are saying, or we are talking about

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן's list of three cases where the רוב is treated as ודאי (מקור, שליא, חתיכה) is limited to טומאה. Cases of איסור, like תשע חנויות, are outside his list.

phrases.english: We are talking about impurity,
we are not talking about prohibition.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 10 by limiting the scope of רבי יוחנן's list.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of the original statement
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יוחנן's list seemed to claim it covered every case of following the רוב as ודאי.
steps.terutzMaskana: The list covers only cases of טומאה. The nine-stores case is about איסור, so it does not contradict the list.

steps.title: The nine frogs and one creeping animal
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי יוחנן's list with another טומאה case where we follow the רוב: nine dead frogs and one dead שרץ.
steps.simpleTranslation: But there is another case! Nine dead frogs and one dead שרץ are lying together. Someone touched one of them and does not know which one. In a רשות היחיד his doubt makes him impure, and in a רשות הרבים his doubt leaves him pure. And if one of them was separated and found somewhere else, we follow the majority.
steps.whatsHappening: Step 11 said רבי יוחנן only listed cases of טומאה. Now the גמרא brings a case that really is about טומאה, where we also follow the רוב, so it seems it should be on his list.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Dead frogs do not make a person impure, but a dead שרץ does. When one creature is found away from the group, we say it most likely came from the majority, the frogs, so it is pure. That is a טומאה ruling based on רוב, so why did רבי יוחנן leave it out?

keyTerms.meaning: Frog. A dead frog does not make a person impure.
One of the creeping animals whose dead body makes a person impure.
A private area. Here, a doubt about טומאה is ruled impure.
A public area. Here, a doubt about טומאה is ruled pure.
His doubt, meaning the unclear case.

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two parts. When he touched one of the ten while they were all still together, we do NOT follow the רוב; we go by private or public area. Only a creature found by itself, away from the group, follows the רוב.

phrases.english: But isn't there the case of nine frogs
phrases.notes: These are dead frogs, which don't make anyone impure. A dead שרץ does.

phrases.english: and one creeping animal among them,
and he touched one of them,
and he does not know which of them he touched:
in a private area, his doubt is impure;
in a public area, his doubt is pure;
and with one that is found,
phrases.notes: This means one creature was separated from the group and found somewhere else, and he touched it there.

phrases.english: follow the majority!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of Step 11, which narrowed רבי יוחנן's list to טומאה cases.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's list of exactly three cases, even after it was limited to טומאה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The frogs-and-שרץ case is a טומאה case where a found item follows the רוב, so the list should have included it.

steps.title: The list covers only a woman's impurity
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רבי יוחנן only listed cases about a woman's טומאה, not טומאה in general.
steps.simpleTranslation: We are talking about the טומאה of a woman. We are not talking about טומאה in general.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the frogs question by making רבי יוחנן's list even narrower. It only covers טומאה that has to do with a woman.
steps.deeperAnalysis: All three cases on the list, מקור, שליא and חתיכה, are about a woman's body and birth or blood. The frogs case is about טומאה from touching a dead creature. So it is real טומאה, but not a woman's טומאה, and it does not belong on the list.

keyTerms.meaning: Impurity connected to a woman, like from blood or giving birth.
Impurity in general, from any source.

steps.whatToRemember: After Steps 11 and 13, רבי יוחנן's list means: cases of a woman's טומאה where חכמים followed the רוב as if it were certain.

phrases.english: We are speaking about the impurity of a woman;
we are not speaking about impurity in general.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the scope of the original statement
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יוחנן's list should include every טומאה case that follows the רוב.
steps.terutzMaskana: The list only covers a woman's טומאה, so the frogs case is left out.

steps.title: A new challenge: the woman who crossed a river
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא starts another challenge to the list, from a teaching of רבי יהושע בן לוי about a woman who crossed a river.
steps.simpleTranslation: But there is what רבי יהושע בן לוי said: a woman who crossed a river...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a new challenge. It starts quoting a teaching of רבי יהושע בן לוי, and the rest of the case continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This time the case is about a woman, so the answer from Step 13 won't help. If this case also follows the רוב, it seems it should be on רבי יוחנן's list.

keyTerms.meaning: She crossed or passed over.
River.

phrases.english: But isn't there this:
what Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:
if she crossed a river

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָאִיכָּא הָא דְּאָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After Step 13 limited the list to a woman's טומאה, this begins a challenge from a case that is about a woman.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's list, now limited to a woman's טומאה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יהושע בן לוי's case is about a woman, so if it follows the רוב, the list seems incomplete.
